# estimation.backtest { #wdm.estimation.backtest }

`estimation.backtest`

Out-of-sample check: how well does the fitted model forecast the scale?

Synthetic recovery tests the inference machinery on data the model generated
itself. It cannot say whether the model describes a person. This module asks
the question that can: replaying each episode day by day, with the filter
knowing only what had happened by then, how close were its forecasts of the
next reading, and of the reading a week later, and were its stated intervals
honest?

For every origin day ``j`` and horizon ``h`` whose target day ``j + h`` has a
weigh-in, the filtered belief on the morning of ``j`` is pushed through ``h``
unscented time updates, driven by the food logged on days ``j`` to
``j + h - 1``, with no measurement updates. The resulting predictive
distribution of the reading is scored against what the scale said. Using the
*logged* inputs isolates model error from adherence: the question is whether
the model predicts the scale given what was eaten, not whether the plan was
followed.

Two caveats are part of the result, not footnotes:

* Phase 1 noise scales are fitted on the whole record, so the forecast
  intervals have seen a little of the future. The effect is small (three
  scalars) but makes coverage slightly optimistic.
* Forecasts from neighbouring origins overlap, so at ``h = 7`` the effective
  sample is several times smaller than the count suggests.

The yardstick is persistence: tomorrow's reading equals the last one. A model
that cannot beat it at a week is not earning its complexity.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Forecast](#wdm.estimation.backtest.Forecast) | One scored forecast of a scale reading, in kg. |
| [HorizonScore](#wdm.estimation.backtest.HorizonScore) | Summary of all forecasts at one horizon. Errors in lb. |

### Forecast { #wdm.estimation.backtest.Forecast }

```python
estimation.backtest.Forecast(
    episode,
    origin,
    horizon,
    predicted_kg,
    sd_kg,
    observed_kg,
    persistence_kg,
)
```

One scored forecast of a scale reading, in kg.

### HorizonScore { #wdm.estimation.backtest.HorizonScore }

```python
estimation.backtest.HorizonScore(
    horizon,
    n,
    bias_lb,
    rmse_lb,
    persistence_rmse_lb,
    z_sd,
    coverage50,
    coverage90,
    log_score,
)
```

Summary of all forecasts at one horizon. Errors in lb.

#### Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [skill](#wdm.estimation.backtest.HorizonScore.skill) | Fractional RMSE improvement over persistence; positive is better. |

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [backtest](#wdm.estimation.backtest.backtest) | Score the filter's ``h``-day-ahead forecasts of every weigh-in. |

### backtest { #wdm.estimation.backtest.backtest }

```python
estimation.backtest.backtest(
    episodes,
    cfg,
    noise,
    *,
    horizons=(1, 7),
    dof=None,
    substeps=4,
    param_drift=PARAM_DRIFT_PER_DAY,
    spec=None,
)
```

Score the filter's ``h``-day-ahead forecasts of every weigh-in.

``noise`` should come from phase 1 fitted with the same ``dof``.
